title: Mike Macdonald Hails Sam Darnold’s Progress: “Everything’s Positive,” Yet No Official Deal Confirmed
body:
Seattle’s offensive outlook brightened on Monday when head coach Mike Macdonald reaffirmed his optimism that quarterback Sam Darnold will be back on the field for the team’s Week 12 matchup. The comment, delivered at the first practice after the Seahawks’ bye week, signals that the franchise is moving closer to a decision on the former New York Jets and Carolina Panthers signal‑caller, who has missed the past six games with a lingering shoulder injury. While no official roster move has been announced, Macdonald’s upbeat tone suggests that the coaching staff believes Darnold’s recovery is on schedule and that his return could provide the spark Seattle needs to revive a stagnant offense.

The Seahawks entered the bye at 2‑4, struggling to generate consistent production from the quarterback position. Darnold, acquired in the offseason to replace the departed Russell Wilson, has posted modest numbers: a 67.9 percent completion rate, 2,091 passing yards, six touchdowns and eight interceptions through six starts. Injuries to key offensive weapons—including star tight end Tyler Kelley and wide receiver DK Metcalf—have compounded the challenges, leaving the team reliant on a run‑heavy scheme that has often stalled in the red zone. Macdonald’s confidence, therefore, carries weight; a healthy Darnold could finally unlock the passing game that has been underutilized.

Medical reports indicate that Darnold’s left shoulder, which suffered a Grade 2 sprain during the Week 6 loss to the Detroit Lions, has responded well to a regimen of rest, physical therapy and a gradual throwing program. The team’s sports medicine director, Dr. Jenna Miller, told reporters that the quarterback “has met all the milestones we set for a return to full activity” and that “there are no red flags at this point.” However, she cautioned that the final decision will hinge on how Darnold feels during full‑speed drills, especially when taking snaps under simulated pressure. The timing aligns with Seattle’s upcoming schedule, which pits the Seahawks against the Arizona Cardinals—a defense that, while solid, is not among the league’s elite pass rushes—offering a relatively low‑risk environment for a tentative comeback.

If Darnold does suit up, the strategic implications for Seattle are significant. Offensive coordinator Dave Rogers has been experimenting with play‑action and short‑zone concepts designed to accommodate Darnold’s quick‑release style and mitigate his limited mobility. The coaching staff hopes to blend these schemes with the emerging talent of rookie running back Jaxon Harris, whose burst has already shown promise in the backfield. Moreover, a healthy Darnold could re‑establish a deeper connection with the receiving corps, particularly with rookie wideout Jaxon Cole, who has yet to see a full season of snaps. The potential synergy could help Seattle move away from a one‑dimensional attack that has allowed opponents to stack the box and stifle the run.

Critics, however, remain cautious. Some analysts point out that Darnold’s previous injury history—most notably a torn ACL in 2021—raises questions about his durability over a full 17‑game stretch. Additionally, the Seahawks’ offensive line, still recovering from injuries to left tackle Charles Cunningham and guard Luke Watson, may struggle to protect a quarterback who is not yet fully confident in his shoulder. The risk of re‑injury could force Seattle into a revolving door at the position, a scenario the front office is eager to avoid as they approach the trade deadline.

Looking ahead, the next few weeks will be pivotal for Seattle’s playoff aspirations. A timely return for Darnold could revitalize a stagnant offense, provide a morale boost heading into the crucial second half of the season, and give coach Macdonald a tangible asset to build around. Conversely, if setbacks arise, the Seahawks may need to double down on a run‑first identity or explore alternative options via the trade market. For now, the optimism expressed by Macdonald offers a hopeful narrative for a fan base that has endured a roller‑coaster start, and the league will be watching closely to see whether the quarterback’s comeback materializes on the field.
